bib.title: Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Overview, Chapter 3: Policy-based RL

question: How can a policy be optimised directly, via policy gradients, actor-critic, trust-region/policy-improvement, off-policy, gradient-free and RL-as-inference methods?
contributions: Unified derivation from likelihood-ratio gradient through baselines, GAE, natural gradient, TRPO/PPO/V-MPO, off-policy V-trace, DPG/DDPG/TD3/WPO, to MPO/AWR/SAC via control as inference.

results.claim: The policy gradient theorem rewrites the trajectory-level score-function gradient as an expectation over discounted state visitation and the Q function.
results.setup: Discounted infinite-horizon MDP, gamma<1; Eq 3.24-3.25, grad J = 1/(1-gamma) E_{p_gamma(s) pi(a|s)}[Q grad log pi]; derivation cited to Kakade-Langford 2002
results.quote: This is known as the policy gradient theorem [Sut+99].

results.claim: Any baseline b(s) with E[grad b(s)]=0 leaves the policy gradient unbiased; b=V(s) is the common choice and turns Q into the advantage.
results.setup: Eq 3.26-3.28; V(s) valid if the policy used in it is a frozen copy independent of theta
results.quote: Any function that satisfies E [∇θb(s)] = 0 is a valid baseline.

results.claim: Reward-to-go: dropping rewards that precede action k removes zero-mean terms and cuts variance without bias.
results.setup: Eq 3.7-3.17 expand the product of score and return and cancel terms where reward at k cannot depend on future actions
results.quote: The likelihood ratio estimator can have high variance, since we are sampling entire trajectories.

results.claim: A2C uses the one-step TD error as a single-sample advantage; update is on-policy.
results.setup: Eq 3.32-3.33, Alg 5; target y_t = r_t + gamma(1-done)V_w(s_{t+1}) with stop-gradient
results.quote: This method is therefore called advantage actor critic or A2C.

results.claim: Shared actor-critic loss combines TD loss, policy gradient term and entropy bonus; PopArt normalises the loss scales so lambda weights can stay fixed.
results.setup: Eq 3.34-3.38, shared network with value and policy heads
results.quote: To handle the dynamically varying scales of the different loss functions, we can use the PopArt method of

results.claim: GAE is an exponentially weighted average of n-step advantages with recursion A_t = delta_t + gamma lambda A_{t+1}; lambda trades bias for variance.
results.setup: Eq 3.45-3.47, Alg 6; w_n = lambda^(n-1); A^(1) high bias/low variance, A^(inf) unbiased/high variance
results.quote: Here λ ∈[0, 1] is a parameter that controls the bias-variance tradeoff: larger values decrease the bias but increase the variance.

results.claim: The general estimator sum_t Psi_t grad log pi can use MC return, MC with baseline, advantage, Q, or TD residual as Psi_t.
results.quote: where Ψt may be any of the following:

results.claim: Two-timescale actor-critic: let the critic learn faster so it tracks the current policy; phasic policy gradient alternates the two updates.
results.setup: No experiment given; cites bilevel optimisation literature and Cobbe et al. 2020
results.quote: However, it is better to let critic Vw learn using a faster learning rate (or more updates)

results.claim: Natural gradient replaces Euclidean distance with a KL constraint approximated by the Fisher matrix, giving update delta = -eta F^-1 g.
results.setup: Eq 3.57-3.63; step size eta_k = sqrt(epsilon / g^T F^-1 g); empirical Fisher (3.64-3.66) as cheap approximation
results.quote: The term F−1g is called the natural gradient.

results.claim: Natural policy gradient/actor-critic uses the advantage-weighted score as g_kt, F_k as the mean outer product, and solves F^-1 g by conjugate gradient (Hessian-free); K-FAC is a more accurate alternative.
results.source: Kakade 2001; Rajeswaran et al. 2017; Martens & Grosse 2015; Wu et al. 2017
results.quote: We can compute F−1k gk without having to invert Fk by using the conjugate gradient method

results.claim: Separate actor and critic networks may beat a shared trunk for MLP/CNN agents.
results.setup: MLPs/CNNs; no numbers given in the chapter
results.quote: argue that it can be better to use different networks for the actor and critic

results.claim: Deterministic policy gradient theorem: grad J = E[ grad_theta mu(s) grad_a Q(s,a)|a=mu(s) ]; integrates over states only, so lower variance, but needs off-policy exploration.
results.setup: Eq 3.69-3.73; continuous actions only; off-policy version drops a grad_theta Q term as in Degris et al. 2012
results.quote: The deterministic policy gradient theorem [Sil+14] tells us that the gradient of this expression is given

results.claim: DPG is a DQN analogue for continuous actions and needs no importance sampling in actor or critic updates.
results.quote: Thus we can think of the resulting method as a version of DQN designed for continuous actions.

results.claim: DDPG learns Q with DQN machinery (replay buffer, target network) and trains the actor to maximise Q(s, mu(s)).
results.quote: uses the DQN

results.claim: TD3 adds target policy smoothing, clipped double Q (min over two critics) and delayed policy updates to DDPG.
results.setup: Eq 3.79-3.80, Alg 8; noise clipped to [-c,c] in target action
results.quote: extends DDPG in 3 main ways.

results.claim: Wasserstein policy optimisation (WPO) gives a DPG-like update for stochastic policies, preconditioned by the Fisher matrix; diagonal Gaussian makes F cheap.
results.setup: Eq 3.81-3.83; policy diagonal Gaussian; critic updated DQN-style
results.quote: This is fast to compute and invert.

results.claim: Policy improvement lower bound: J(pi)-J(pi_k) >= surrogate L(pi,pi_k) minus a TV penalty weighted by 2 gamma C/(1-gamma)^2.
results.setup: Eq 3.85; C = max_s |E_pi[A_pik]|; trust-region form 3.86 constrains E[TV] <= epsilon
results.quote: Then one can show [Ach+17] that

results.claim: A KL bound delta implies the TV constraint with delta = epsilon^2/2 (Pinsker-style link used by TRPO and V-MPO).
results.quote: then π also satisfies the TV constraint with δ = ϵ2

results.claim: TRPO: first-order expansion of the surrogate, second-order expansion of the KL, natural-gradient step with eta=sqrt(2 delta / v^T F v), conjugate gradient, then backtracking line search.
results.setup: Eq 3.87-3.90; Fisher approximated as g g^T
results.quote: We then use a backtracking line search procedure to ensure the trust region is satisfied.

results.claim: PPO objective is min(rho A, clip(rho,1-eps,1+eps) A) with multiple minibatch/epoch updates per rollout; derived as a simplification of the TV constraint (E[TV] = 1/2 E|ratio-1|).
results.setup: Eq 3.91-3.92, Alg 9 with GAE; support of pi must lie within support of pi_k
results.quote: which is a simplification of TRPO.

results.claim: PPO clip simplifies to min(rho A, (1+eps)A) when A>=0 and min(rho A, (1-eps)A) when A<0.
results.setup: Eq 3.93-3.95; from OpenAI Spinning Up
results.quote: we can combine these two cases by defining

results.claim: PPO needs action likelihoods, hard for diffusion policies; DPPO treats denoising steps as an inner MDP, NCDPO fixes noise and backpropagates through the chain.
results.setup: Diffusion policies; Ren et al. 2024, Yang et al. 2025
results.quote: The PPO algorithm relies on being able to compute the likelihood of a candidate action.

results.claim: V-MPO is on-policy EM: E step reweights samples by exp(A/lambda*)/Z with lambda* from a dual; M step is weighted max likelihood under a KL trust region; reversed KL makes it mode-covering.
results.quote: Note that here the KL is reversed compared to TRPO in Section 3.3.2.

results.claim: Off-policy evaluation by importance sampling is unbiased; per-decision IS lowers variance.
results.setup: Eq 3.104-3.108; ratio of trajectory probs reduces to product of pi/pi_b
results.quote: It can be verified that Eπb

results.claim: V-trace truncates importance weights with c (trace cutting) and rho (fixed-point choice); best c=1 reported by IMPALA.
results.setup: IMPALA (Espeholt et al. 2018), Eq 3.111-3.113; Atari/DMLab-scale setting not described in this chapter
results.quote: In [Esp+18], they find c = 1 works best.

results.claim: V-trace rho=1 reported best; rho->inf gives V^pi and rho->0 gives V^b.
results.setup: Same as above
results.quote: In [Esp+18], they find ρ = 1 works best.

results.claim: V-trace variance stays bounded only if off-policy replay data is mixed with fresh on-policy data.
results.setup: Analysis of V-trace variance, Schmitt/Hessel/Simonyan 2020
results.quote: They show that to keep this bounded, it is necessary to mix some off-policy data

results.claim: IMPALA trained one agent on all 57 Atari games and beat A3C thanks to off-policy corrections.
results.setup: IMPALA shared CNN+LSTM for value and policy; no scores quoted in this chapter
results.quote: to play all 57 games at a high level.

results.claim: Off-policy PPO/TRPO/V-MPO: generalise the lower bound to any reference policy (mixture of past policies) and use V-trace-style advantage with truncated ratios.
results.setup: Eq 3.121-3.123 (Generalized PPO)
results.quote: The key insight is to realize that we can generalize the lower bound in Equation (3.85) to any reference

results.claim: Gradient-free policy search (CEM, ES, random search, EGGROLL) handles non-differentiable policies and avoids poor local optima of gradient methods.
results.setup: Brief survey, no numbers
results.quote: gradient descent cannot be applied to non-differentiable policies

results.claim: RL as inference adds optimality variables with p(O=1|s,a) proportional to exp(G/eta), enabling off-policy learning without importance sampling; chapter links it to MPO, SAC, SMC planning and LLM test-time inference.
results.setup: Eq 3.124; G may be R, Q or A; Fig 3.3. LLM link is a forward pointer to Sec 6.2.4.11, not developed in this chapter
results.note: The text breaks across lines: 'some kinds of LLM test-time inference, as discussed in Section 6.2.4.11'
results.quote: and some kinds of LLM

results.claim: Policy learning as variational inference: with q using true dynamics, the ELBO is sum_t E_q[G/eta - KL(pi_q || pi_p)], avoiding optimism bias.
results.setup: Eq 3.127-3.135, following Levine 2018
results.quote: Since DKL (q(τ) ∥pπ(τ|O = 1)) ≥0, we see that log p(O = 1|π) ≥J(pπ, q); hence J is called the evidence

results.claim: EM control: E step gives q(a|s) proportional to pi_prev(a|s) exp(G/eta); M step is weighted maximum likelihood.
results.quote: which we recognize as a weighted maximum likelihood problem.

results.claim: KL control with uniform prior and G=R gives the maximum entropy RL objective R - eta H.
results.quote: This is called the maximum entropy RL objective

results.claim: MPO is EM control with G=Q (Retrace or one-step Bellman); eta found by minimising a dual; M step adds a Gaussian prior around previous params (Fisher-scaled), equal to a KL trust region.
results.setup: Eq 3.143-3.149; Z(s) estimated by Monte Carlo with M samples from the prior policy
results.quote: This is an instance of EM control, where

results.claim: AWR uses G=A (GAE advantages, TD(lambda) values); AWAC uses G=Q (TD(0)); both are EM control with closed-form E step and temperature as a hyperparameter.
results.source: Peng et al. 2019; Nair et al. 2020
results.quote: are both EM control methods.

results.claim: SAC is off-policy actor-critic for max-entropy RL, with policy update through the actor's own distribution so no importance sampling is needed.
results.setup: Eq 3.150-3.152; objective R + alpha H
results.quote: eliminating the need to use importance

results.claim: Optimal soft policy in the tabular case is a softmax over Q/alpha and V* = alpha log sum exp(Q*/alpha).
results.setup: Eq 3.153-3.161, derived with a Lagrange multiplier
results.quote: The optimal policy is therefore the softmax over Q-values:

results.claim: SAC uses two soft Q networks with min target and EMA target networks; REDQ uses N>=2 networks.
results.quote: suggest fitting two soft Q functions

results.claim: SAC policy loss J = E[alpha log pi - Q] is optimised with the reparameterisation trick (lower variance than REINFORCE); Gumbel-softmax or SAC-Discrete for discrete actions.
results.setup: Eq 3.166-3.168, Alg 11; Gaussian policy
results.quote: The latter is much lower variance, so is preferable.

results.claim: SAC temperature alpha can be tuned automatically toward a target entropy H.
results.setup: J(alpha) = E[-alpha (log pi + H_target)]; H_target is a hyperparameter
results.quote: to automatically adjust the temperature parameter

results.claim: Active inference minimises expected free energy, splitting into epistemic and extrinsic terms; related to control as inference when p(o) proportional to exp R(o).
results.quote: Control as inference is closely related to a technique known as active inference

limits: Survey chapter: no experiments of its own; every number is a hyperparameter or count taken from other work.
Chapter says it omits network implementation details (activations, LayerNorm) and does not tackle epistemic uncertainty/exploration in RL-as-inference.
LLM/RLHF use (GRPO, DPO, token-level MDP) is not in this chapter; only a forward pointer to LLM test-time inference in Sec 6.2.4.11. Figure 3.2 credit line contains a stray 'foo'.
Algorithm 8 writes the policy loss with a square, (Q(s,mu(s)))^2, which looks like a typo; Alg 8 calls update-actor while the loop calls update-policy.
Eq 3.8 and some equation text have typos in the source (e.g. 'r + 3 gamma^2').
practices: Use V(s) as the baseline to reduce variance (Sec 3.1.5).
Add an entropy term to actor-critic losses to keep the policy stochastic (Sec 3.2.1).
Use a stop-gradient on the TD target (Sec 3.2.1).
Use PopArt to normalise TD, PG and entropy loss scales when sharing a network (Sec 3.2.1, 3.2.5).
Let the critic learn faster than the actor (two timescale) (Sec 3.2.3).
Use conjugate gradient instead of inverting the Fisher matrix (Sec 3.2.4.2).
For off-policy actor-critic, use V-trace with c=1 and rho=1 as reported by IMPALA (Sec 3.4.2.1).
Mix off-policy replay data with fresh on-policy data to bound V-trace variance (Sec 3.4.2.1).
Prefer the reparameterisation trick over REINFORCE for SAC's actor update (Sec 3.6.8.4).
Use clipped double Q (min of two critics) to counter overestimation in TD3 and SAC (Sec 3.2.6.3, 3.6.8.3).

terms.definition: grad J = E[grad log p_theta(tau) R(tau)]; grad log pi is the (Fisher) score function
G_k = r_k + gamma r_{k+1} + ... , the return from step k
policy gradient where the expected return is estimated by TD learning of a value function instead of MC rollouts
methods that try to monotonically improve performance of the policy at each step
F^-1 g, the gradient preconditioned by the inverse Fisher information matrix
O_t indicating whether the action at time t is optimal, p(O_t=1|s,a) proportional to exp(G/eta)
two ways to solve the ELBO: EM alternates non-parametric E and parametric M steps; KL control optimises only the variational policy
standard RL objective plus an entropy regulariser on the policy
